title: Gloss Real Drops Document
description: Controls how Gloss presents dropped items: BlockDisplay models for placeable materials, ItemDisplay models for true items, tumble and landing, labels, typed keyframe animation, and optional scripted and physics layers. The document lives at plugins/Gloss/real-drops/default.json and is hot reloaded. Documentation grade only: the Java parser (RealDropSettingsDoc) is the format's source of truth and clamps every numeric value at load.

schemaVersion.description: Document format version. Must be exactly 1; any other value is rejected outright rather than migrated.

revision.description: Server-owned monotonic revision counter. Starts at 1 and increases every time the server rewrites the document; editors must send back the revision they read so a concurrent change is detected instead of silently overwritten.

limits.description: Update cadence and per-chunk budget. These are the knobs that decide how much work the presentation costs; raising the visual counts multiplies the number of display entities on screen.

scale.description: Base display size per model shape. Every dropped item falls into one of three shape families and takes the matching scale, which the script layer's scale block then multiplies.

motion.description: Mid-air tumble. Applies while the item is falling; once it lands the landing block takes over.

landing.description: The resting pose an item settles into once it touches the ground.

labels.description: The floating TextDisplay name drawn above a dropped stack.

filters.description: Which drops get a presentation at all. A filtered-out item keeps its ordinary vanilla appearance.

physics.description: Real changes to how the dropped Item entity moves, not just how it looks. Disabled by default. These knobs write to the entity's velocity and gravity flag, so they move the item's real position and its pickup hitbox with it. They only apply while the item has a Gloss presentation: a filtered-out or ineligible drop falls exactly as vanilla does.

script.description: The scripted presentation layer: expression strings compiled once when the document loads. Expressions without index are shared by the stack, and static settled plans are not reevaluated until their inputs change. Disabled by default, and additive - it composes on top of everything the scale, motion and landing blocks already computed rather than replacing it. Script results move the DISPLAY only; the item entity, its collision and its pickup radius stay where Minecraft put them. Use the physics block when the item itself must move.

animation.description: Typed keyframe animation profiles selected by material. Clips are triggered by lifecycle events and physical phases, then compose scalar display, physics-gate, glow and temporary-light outputs. Disabled by default and independent of the advanced script layer.

updateIntervalTicks.description: Ticks between presentation updates while an item is moving. Lower is smoother and more expensive. Clamped to 1-20, default 2.

settledPollIntervalTicks.description: Ticks between updates once an item has come to rest. A settled item is not re-posed, so this can be much slower than the moving interval. Clamped to 2-200, default 20. The physics block forces the faster moving interval while an item is in water, since a buoyant item is never really at rest.

maxVisualsPerStack.description: Upper bound on the number of display models drawn for one dropped stack. Larger stacks earn more models up to this cap: 1 model below 2 items, 2 up to 16, 3 up to 32, 4 up to 48, then the cap. Clamped to 1-5, default 3.

maxVisualsPerChunk.description: Total display entities Gloss will spawn for drops in a single chunk, labels included. Once the budget is exhausted further drops in that chunk keep their vanilla look until room frees up. Clamped to 8-1024, default 128.

viewRange.description: Distance in blocks at which the item models stop rendering for a client. Clamped to 4-128, default 32. A script whose visible expression is false hides a display by driving its view range to zero.

spread.description: How far the extra models of a multi-model stack sit from the first one, as a fraction of the authored offsets. 0 stacks them all in one place. Clamped to 0-1, default 0.18.

defaultScale.description: Display size for full block items such as STONE. Clamped to 0.05-2, default 0.4.

flatItems.description: Display size for non-block items rendered through ItemDisplay. Placeable materials use BlockDisplay even when their inventory icon is flat. Clamped to 0.05-2, default 0.65.

thinBlocks.description: Display size for slabs, carpets, pressure plates and snow. Clamped to 0.05-2, default 0.45.

tumble.description: Whether an airborne item spins. Turn this off for items that should fall flat and still. Default true.

speedMultiplier.description: Multiplies all three tumble rates at once. Clamped to 0.1-4, default 1.35.

degreesPerSecondX.description: Base pitch tumble rate in degrees per second, before variance and the speed multiplier. Clamped to -1440 to 1440, default 160.

degreesPerSecondY.description: Base yaw tumble rate in degrees per second. Clamped to -1440 to 1440, default 120.

degreesPerSecondZ.description: Base roll tumble rate in degrees per second. Clamped to -1440 to 1440, default 100.

variance.description: How much the per-item tumble rate is allowed to wander from the configured base, as a fraction. 0 makes every item spin identically; the direction of each axis is still chosen per item. Clamped to 0-1, default 0.2.

changeOnBounce.description: Whether an item re-rolls its tumble rates each time it bounces. Default true. The bounces script variable counts those bounces whether or not this is on.

velocityInfluence.description: How strongly real linear speed increases airborne angular speed. Clamped to 0-4, default 0.35.

submergedSpinMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to angular motion while submerged. Clamped to 0-1, default 0.35.

groundRollMultiplier.description: Scales rotation generated from actual supported travel. 0 slides; 1 rolls at the natural model radius. Clamped to 0-4, default 1.

mode.description: The resting pose. NATURAL rolls block items onto whichever face is nearest the ground and gives everything else a small random tilt; FLAT lays every item face-up; UPRIGHT stands every item on end. Default NATURAL.

tiltDegrees.description: Maximum random lean, in degrees, applied to a resting item in NATURAL mode. 0 makes every landing perfectly square. Clamped to 0-45, default 10.

randomYaw.description: Whether each item gets its own resting yaw, so a pile of the same drop does not look cloned. Default true.

transitionTicks.description: Client interpolation length for continuous pose samples. Clamped to 0-20, default 4.

faceAttraction.description: Fraction of remaining face-alignment angle removed per sample when nearly still. Clamped to 0-1, default 0.55.

movingFaceAttraction.description: Face attraction retained while rolling or sliding. Clamped to 0-1, default 0.15.

alignmentDegrees.description: Subvisual tolerance for the final exact face alignment. Clamped to 0.05-10 degrees, default 0.5.

settleDelayTicks.description: Ticks an aligned, motionless item remains stable before sparse settled polling. Clamped to 0-100, default 4.

enabled.description: Whether the floating name is drawn. When off, the item's own custom name visibility is restored. Default true.

yOffset.description: Height of the label above the item, in blocks. Clamped to 0-4, default 0.55.

scale.description: Text size of the label. Clamped to 0.1-4, default 0.85.

viewRange.description: Distance in blocks at which the label stops rendering. Clamped to 4-128, default 32.

billboard.description: How the label turns to face the viewer. CENTER always faces the camera, HORIZONTAL and VERTICAL pivot on one axis only, FIXED never turns. Default CENTER.

seeThrough.description: Whether the label is visible through blocks. Default true.

shadow.description: Whether the label text is drawn with a drop shadow. Default true.

background.description: Whether the label draws its coloured background plate. When false the plate is fully transparent and the four background channels are ignored. Default true.

backgroundRed.description: Red channel of the label background plate, 0-255. Default 0.

backgroundGreen.description: Green channel of the label background plate, 0-255. Default 0.

backgroundBlue.description: Blue channel of the label background plate, 0-255. Default 0.

backgroundAlpha.description: Opacity of the label background plate, 0-255. Default 80.

disabledWorlds.description: World names, matched case-insensitively, where drops keep their vanilla appearance. Empty means every world is presented.

materialBlacklist.description: Material names, upper case, that are never presented. Defaults to BEDROCK and BARRIER. Setting this key to an empty array really does clear it; omitting the key restores the two defaults.

onlyPlayerDrops.description: When true, only items a player threw or dropped are presented; mob loot, block breaks and dispensers keep their vanilla look. Default false.

enabled.description: Master switch for the physics layer. Default false, and while it is false Gloss never touches the item entity's velocity or gravity flag, so drops fall exactly as vanilla does.

gravityMultiplier.description: Scales how hard a dropped item falls. This is a real change to the entity: at 1 nothing is touched, above 1 Gloss adds extra downward velocity each update, below 1 it adds upward velocity to cancel part of the fall, and exactly 0 clears the entity's gravity flag so the item hangs where it is. Because the correction is applied per update rather than per tick, the effective acceleration is approximate at slow update intervals. Clamped to 0-4, default 1.

bounce.description: Restitution applied when an item lands. Vanilla items do not bounce at all; Gloss detects the landing and rewrites the vertical velocity to the given fraction of the approach speed, so the item really leaves the ground again. Each bounce increments the bounces script variable and, when motion.changeOnBounce is on, re-rolls the tumble. Very small landings below a fixed threshold are ignored so a resting item does not jitter. Clamped to 0-0.9, default 0 (off).

waterBuoyancy.description: Upward velocity added each update while the item is in water, on top of whatever vanilla already does. This is real movement: a buoyant item rises and can be picked up higher in the column. Clamped to 0-1, default 0 (off).

waterDrag.description: Fraction of the item's velocity removed each update while it is in water, applied to all three axes. 0 leaves vanilla water motion alone, 1 stops the item dead the moment it is submerged. Clamped to 0-1, default 0 (off).

enabled.description: Master switch for the script layer. Default false. While it is false every expression here is still parsed and validated when the document loads, so a broken expression is reported immediately, but nothing is evaluated at runtime and the presentation is bit-for-bit what it was before the script block existed.

vars.description: Author-defined intermediate values, written as a name to expression map. They are evaluated first, in the order they appear in the file, and each one is visible to every expression declared after it as well as to offset, rotation, scale, glow and visible. This is what makes non-trivial logic writable: give the condition a name once, then reuse it. Each value must evaluate to a number, so encode a flag as 1 and 0 and test it with a comparison. A name must be a plain identifier, must not repeat, and must not shadow a built-in variable. At most 32 entries.

offset.description: Extra displacement of the display, in blocks, added to the offset the document already computed for this model. Positive Y lifts the model. This moves the picture only: the item entity and its pickup radius do not follow, so a large offset visually detaches the model from the thing a player walks over. Each axis is clamped to -16..16 blocks. Defaults to 0 on every axis.

rotation.description: Extra rotation in degrees, composed onto the pose the tumble and landing blocks produced rather than replacing it, and applied in X then Y then Z order. The resting height correction is recomputed from the final pose, so a scripted rotation of a block item will not sink it into the floor. Each axis is clamped to -3600..3600 degrees. Defaults to 0 on every axis.

scale.description: Multiplier applied to whichever scale family this item resolved to, per axis, so 1 leaves the configured size alone and 2 doubles it. Non-uniform values squash and stretch the model. Each axis is clamped to 0..16; 0 collapses the model to nothing, which is a blunter way of hiding it than the visible expression. Defaults to 1 on every axis.

glow.description: Colour of the display's glowing outline. An empty string turns the whole feature off and is the default. Otherwise it is an expression producing either a colour number (a #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB literal, or rgb()/argb()/mix()/palette()) or a #RRGGBB string; a result of exactly 0 means no glow, which is how a conditional glow is written - for example "materialIs('torch') ? #FFAA55 : 0". Only the red, green and blue channels reach the client; the outline itself is drawn by the client, so it is visible through blocks.

visible.description: Boolean expression gating whether this display is drawn at all. Must evaluate to true or false, not a number. A false result drives the display's view range to zero, which stops clients rendering it; the item entity is untouched and remains pickupable. Defaults to "true".

enabled.description: Master switch for typed animation clips. Disabled by default.

materialProperties.description: Named material-property maps referenced by keyframes. Material keys accept the same * and ? globs as profile matchers; the first matching entry wins.

glow.description: Unsigned ARGB glow value resolved by a GLOW keyframe.

lightLevel.description: Temporary block-light level requested by a LIGHT_LEVEL keyframe. World placement is handled separately from animation evaluation.

profiles.description: Ordered animation profiles. Higher priority wins; declaration order breaks ties.

priority.description: Selection priority. Higher profiles win before declaration order is considered.

materials.description: Material names or * and ? globs. Namespace prefixes are ignored and matching is case-insensitive.

clips.description: State and event clips owned by this profile.

trigger.description: Lifecycle event or physical animation phase that starts or drives this clip.

durationTicks.description: Length of the clip timeline in server ticks.

loop.description: Whether elapsed time wraps at durationTicks.

tracks.description: Ordered scalar tracks. Their blend operations are applied in declaration order.

target.description: Animation output controlled by this scalar track.

blend.description: REPLACE supports every target, ADD supports offsets and rotations, and MULTIPLY supports scale axes.

keyframes.description: Keyframes on this track. Duplicate ticks are rejected and runtime compilation orders them by tick.

tick.description: Position on the containing clip timeline, in server ticks.

value.description: Literal scalar value and fallback when a referenced material map has no match.

materialMap.description: Optional named materialProperties map. Supported by GLOW and LIGHT_LEVEL tracks.

easing.description: Interpolation from the previous keyframe into this keyframe.

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: Three expressions, one per axis. Any axis you leave out or leave blank falls back to the block's neutral value (0 for offset and rotation, 1 for scale).

x.description: Expression for the X axis. X is east in world space.

y.description: Expression for the Y axis. Y is up.

z.description: Expression for the Z axis. Z is south in world space.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description: A string in the Gloss expression language, compiled once when the document loads. Expressions without index are evaluated once per stack, and static settled plans are reused until an input changes. A parse error names the field and character position and refuses the document; a runtime failure logs once and falls back to the neutral field value. Variables include t, age, index, count, amount, onGround, settled, phase, stateTime, impactSpeed, inWater, inLava, bounces, velocityX, velocityY, velocityZ, speed, shape-aware height, blockLight, skyLight, random, material, isBlock, isFlat, isThin and pi. Drop-specific functions are materialIs(name) and materialMatches(glob); the expression grammar and complete standard-library reference are documented in DROP_SCRIPT_FORMAT.md.
